rfi.description: A sweeping package of reforms, passed unanimously by the lower house of parliament this week, aims to overhaul how France investigates and prosecutes sexual violence. Yet campaigners say the legislation does not do enough to prevent abuse, while protection for some of the most vulnerable victims is lacking.

rfi.title: AI midwife seeks to fill gaps in Zimbabwe's maternal health care
rfi.description: With public health services stretched thin, women in Zimbabwe sometimes struggle to access reliable information about pregnancy and childbirth. A locally developed app aims to answer their questions and direct them to appropriate care, in an example of the potential of artificial intelligence to ease pressure on overloaded health systems.

rfi.title: Pacific nations await climate billions, as fossil fuel divide looms over Cop31
rfi.description: Ahead of next month’s United Nations Cop31 climate summit, as a strengthening El Niño drives Pacific sea temperatures towards record levels, more than $5 billion promised to the region remains unpaid. Cop31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia are pushing to speed up the switch to electric transport, heating and industry, but participating countries are divided over how to wind down the use of coal, oil and gas.

rfi.title: Shipping attacks threaten Turkey's resolve to keep warships out of Black Sea
rfi.description: A wave of deadly attacks on cargo ships in the waters of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania has jolted the alliance into calling an emergency meeting on Black Sea security. Yet any move to send NATO ships hinges on Turkey reversing its steadfast refusal to allow warships into the Black Sea.

rfi.title: Zelensky says US move to waive sanctions 'rewards' Russia's Putin

rfi.title: Madagascar marks one year since uprising as Russia’s influence grows
rfi.description: Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through closer military ties and weapons deliveries, while researchers have identified Moscow’s interest in a strategic Indian Ocean port. Many of the political reforms demanded by protesters, however, remain unfinished.

rfi.title: Mayors urge France to recognise 1961 Paris massacre of Algerians as state crime
rfi.description: On the eve of the 65th anniversary of the massacre of Algerian protesters in Paris, French mayors are calling for the events of 17 October, 1961 to be officially recognised as a state crime.

rfi.title: School students called to join Yellow Vests and unions for mass French protest
rfi.description: Following an unsuccessful meeting with France's education minister on Thursday, protesting high school pupils across the country say they will not let up the pressure on the government. The Yellow Vests movement has called on the students to join them at a nationwide demonstration on Saturday over working conditions and the cost of living.

rfi.title: France and Germany strike deal to boost Europe's struggling car industry
rfi.description: France and Germany have agreed a deal to safeguard Europe's automobile industry and stave off fierce competition from Chinese electric car companies. The agreement also opens the door for the United Kingdom to be treated as a trusted partner under "Made in EU" rules.

Son objectif : faire voter, le 3 novembre, lors d’un référendum, une mesure qui permettrait d’imposer ponctuellement 5 % du patrimoine des milliardaires qui résident dans cet Etat. france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Emmanuel Macron va s'adresser "solennellement" aux Français à 20 h
Russie-Ukraine : nouvelles frappes croisées sur le système énergétique
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes croisées ont touché des cibles énergétiques en Russie et en Ukraine dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche, causant notamment un impressionnant incendie sur un site pétrolier à Saint-Pétersbourg et privant d'électricité des dizaines de milliers de personnes.

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : 800 000 participants en France, selon un bilan actualisé
france24fr.description: Quelque 800.000 personnes ont participé aux actions et défilés partout en France samedi contre la "vie chère", selon un bilan actualisé diffusé par plusieurs organisations associées à cette mobilisation nationale.

france24fr.title: 17 octobre : pillages, chaos, les forces de l'ordre dépassées ?
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu est dimanche la ⁠cible de critiques ​sur sa gestion du maintien de l'ordre au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la ​vie chère dans toute la France.

france24fr.title: Violences à Paris : plus de 500 personnes en garde à vue, annonce le parquet
france24fr.description: Plus de 500 personnes (517) sont en garde à vue dimanche après les violences et pillages commises samedi à Paris, plus précisément 346 personnes majeures et 171 mineurs, a indiqué le parquet de la capitale dans un bilan "pas encore consolidé".

france24fr.title: Quand le climat menace le patrimoine, 20 sites français en danger
france24fr.description: Benjamin Crettenand, chargé de la sensibilisation au changement climatique, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 17 octobre : comme un air de 2018 dans de nombreuses villes
france24fr.description: Le jour s'est levé dimanche sur un spectacle de désolation dans les rues des principales villes de France, au lendemain du chaos qui a éclipsé la mobilisation contre la "vie chère", à six mois de la présidentielle.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 17 octobre : le gouvernement français débordé ?
france24fr.description: Patrick Bruneteaux, spécialiste des questions de maintien de l'ordre en France, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: France, Albanie, Belgique : la colère des jeunes gronde en Europe
france24fr.description: Les affrontements se sont poursuivis samedi pour le cinquième jour à Tirana où les manifestants exigent la démission du chef du gouvernement albanais et dénoncent les conditions d'enseignement et les droits d'inscription universitaires. D'autres violents affrontements ont eu lieu dans de multiples villes d'Europe.

france24fr.title: Midterms : manifestations "No Kings" dans plusieurs villes des Etats-Unis
france24fr.description: Loïc Piallat, notre correspondant à Los Angeles, décrypte la situation.

france24fr.title: La France sonnée au lendemain d'une journée de mobilisation ayant viré au chaos
france24fr.description: La France constate l'ampleur des dégâts dimanche matin après les violences, les pillages et le chaos qui ont éclipsé la mobilisation contre la "vie chère", à six mois de la présidentielle.

La chute de Fernando Cerimedo, le sulfureux consultant au cœur des droites latino-américaines
france24fr.description: Connu pour avoir conseillé des hommes politiques comme Javier Milei et Jair Bolsonaro, l’Argentin Fernando Cerimedo est poursuivi en Bolivie pour "tentative de féminicide" sur son ex-compagne. zeit.title: Lisz Hirn: »Höre nicht nur auf dich selbst!«
zeit.description: Wir sind so gehorsam wie noch nie, schreibt die österreichische Philosophin Lisz Hirn. Dabei kommt der Mensch mit einer anderen Strategie viel weiter.

zeit.description: Unionsfraktionschef Frei moniert Ungerechtigkeiten im Gesundheitssystem. So müssten auch gesetzlich Versicherte »in vertretbarer Frist einen Facharzttermin bekommen«.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Berliner Linkspartei siegt über die mutlose politische Mitte: Dieses Sondierungspapier ist eine Zäsur für Deutschland
nzz.description: SPD und Grüne wollten mit der Linkspartei nur dann verhandeln, wenn eine Koalition unter ihrer Führung «nicht von Antisemiten abhängig» sei. Von diesem Vorsatz ist nichts mehr übrig. Das hat Folgen, auch über Berlin hinaus.

nzz.title: Mit 36 km/h durch den Wald brettern: In Bern werden erstmals die Schweizer Meister im Trendsport Graveln gekürt
nzz.description: Immer mehr Velofahrerinnen und Velofahrer suchen auf Schotterwegen Freiheit und Abenteuer. Nun entdeckt auch der Spitzensport die Disziplin.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Drohne in litauischen Luftraum eingedrungen und abgestürzt +++ Massiver Drohnenangriff auf St. Petersburg
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Angriffe im Westjordanland bringen Benjamin Netanyahu in Bedrängnis
nzz.description: Radikale israelische Siedler sollen eine amerikanische Journalistin und europäische Diplomaten attackiert haben. Selbst enge Verbündete Israels reagieren empört.

nzz.title: Ukrainische Schläge gegen Rechenzentren: Die Angriffe auf Yandex treffen Russlands Online-Wirtschaft ins Mark
nzz.description: Die russische Tech-Firma Yandex beherrscht den Markt. Das ist politisch gewollt – und macht Yandex zu einem formidablen Ziel für die Ukraine.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Helene Fischer bringt noch 2026 ein neues Album heraus
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

Brände, Plünderungen und Verwüstungen – und die Schüler spielten bei den Krawallen nur noch eine Nebenrolle
nzz.description: Gelbwesten, Gewerkschafter, Studenten und andere Gruppen hatten am Samstag einen gemeinsamen Protesttag organisiert. Er wurde von massiven Ausschreitungen und Zerstörungen überschattet. Der Premierminister spricht von einem «entsetzlichen Ausmass von Gewalt».

nzz.title: Ein Feuer auf einem kanadischen Militärstützpunkt fordert mehrere Tote
nzz.description: Der Stützpunkt Wainwright ist einer der am stärksten frequentierten Armeestandorte des Landes. Über die Ursache des Feuers und die genaue Opferzahl ist bis anhin nichts bekannt.

nzz.title: «Sie stellen ja nervigere Fragen als die Polizei!»: Mehr als 2000 Maghrebiner tauchten letztes Jahr in der Schweiz unter
nzz.description: Sie haben nichts zu verlieren. Jedes Jahr verschwinden in der Schweiz etliche Algerier, Marokkaner und Tunesier ohne sich bei den Behörden abzumelden. Wo treiben sich diese jungen Männer rum?

nzz.title: Schöner wohnen in Zürich – bald billiger?
nzz.description: Der Wohnungsmarkt in Zürich entspannt sich, teilweise werden sogar die Mieten gesenkt. Braucht es da noch staatliche Interventionen wie ein Airbnb-Verbot?

nzz.title: «Digger» ist der Kino-Flop des Jahres – und in allerbester Gesellschaft
nzz.description: Die Kulturgeschichte ist voller missratener Versuche, Meisterwerke zu erschaffen. Scheitern gehört zum Berufsrisiko des Künstlers. Gut so!

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das Land braucht einen heilsamen Schock: Lasst die AHV-Finanzierung platzen!
nzz.description: Die geplante Mehrwertsteuererhöhung zur Teilfinanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente könnte an der Urne scheitern. Es wäre ein gutes Signal. Wählerbeschenkung nach dem Giesskannenprinzip darf nicht Schule machen – wie die Staatskrisen der klammen Nachbarn beweisen.

spiegel.title: Taiwan: Küstenwache drängt 16 chinesische Schiffe zurück
spiegel.description: Taiwan hat nach eigenen Angaben eine »maritime Belästigung« in ungewöhnlich großem Umfang abgewehrt. Mehr als ein Dutzend chinesischer Schiffe hat sich demnach im Schwarm der Inselrepublik genährt.

spiegel.title: Olfen im Münsterland: Haftbefehl nach Messerattacke in Seniorenheim
spiegel.description: Was brachte einen 72-Jährigen im Rollstuhl dazu, in einem Seniorenheim mutmaßlich mit einem Messer auf Mitbewohnerinnen loszugehen? Eine Frau starb. Im Ort wird für die Opfer gebetet.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Ermittler sammeln Beweise für Kriegsverbrechen an der Natur
spiegel.description: Tote Delfine, brennende Wälder, Angriffe auf Nuklearanlagen: Ukrainische Ermittler sammeln Beweise für ein Verbrechen, das es im Völkerrecht noch nicht gibt: Ökozid. Unterwegs mit der Spezialeinheit der Staatsanwaltschaft.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Warum sich junge Menschen von KI bedroht fühlen
spiegel.description: Sie sind mit Smartphone und Social Media aufgewachsen. Doch auf künstliche Intelligenz reagieren viele junge Menschen inzwischen mit Wut und Unbehagen. Drei von ihnen erzählen, warum.

spiegel.title: China: Neue Meldepflichten für Technologietransfers bei KI und Solarzellen
spiegel.description: KI-Agenten, Solarzellen, Gentherapien – die chinesische Führung will strengere Auflagen für den Export von 40 Schlüsseltechnologien. Das Handelsministerium verweist auf Sicherheitsrisiken.

spiegel.title: So arbeitet ein Glasbläser: Von der Flamme bis zum Feinschliff
spiegel.description: Michael Weinfurtner arbeitet mit heißem Glas. Er lässt Flüssigkeit innerhalb kürzester Zeit erstarren und macht aus ­geschmolzenen Scherben Kunst. Wie funktioniert das?

spiegel.title: Iran: Teheran bestätigt sanktionierten Verteidigungsminister im Amt – Drohungen gegen USA
spiegel.description: In Teheran endet die Hängepartie um die Nachfolge des Verteidigungsministers: Das Parlament billigte den Luftfahrtexperten Mehrdad Achlaki Ketabtschi. Der Iraner ist in der EU und in den USA sanktioniert.

spiegel.title: Energiepreise: Netzentgelte für Strom und Gas steigen 2027 bundesweit leicht
spiegel.description: Strom und Gas werden teurer – aber nicht überall gleich. Die Netzentgelte werden im Jahr 2027 bundesweit höher ausfallen, zeigt eine neue Auswertung. In Hamburg wird es besonders teuer.

spiegel.title: Mailand, Lissabon, Brüssel: Proteste und Krawalle in einigen europäischen Städten
spiegel.description: In Frankreich herrscht Chaos. Auch in Belgien und Italien sind Menschen wegen steigender Lebenshaltungskosten auf ‌die Straßen und Plätze gegangen. In Portugals Hauptstadt Lissabon haben Hunderte ein Protestcamp errichtet.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Randale und Plünderungen im ganzen Land, Marine Le Pen dürfte profitieren
spiegel.description: Wenige Monate bevor Präsident Macron ausscheidet, erschüttert die Gewaltorgie junger Randalierer das Land. Politisch dürfte davon eine Frau profitieren: die rechtsradikale Präsidentschaftsfavoritin Marine Le Pen.

spiegel.title: Future Faking: Wie Sie Flunkerei beim Date und in der Partnerschaft früh erkennen
spiegel.description: Wenn Sie beide von der Zukunft träumen: Sagt Ihr Gegenüber die Wahrheit? Vorsicht vor Menschen, die zu große Versprechen abgeben, empfiehlt Paartherapeutin Sonja Bröning. Hier verrät sie, wie Sie Flunkerei früh erkennen.

spiegel.title: Tanken: Kommt nach der Verbrenner-Einigung jetzt der E20-Kraftstoff?
spiegel.description: Rund 15 Jahre nach der bundesweiten Einführung von E10-Sprit könnte bald der nächste Schritt zu E20 kommen – zumindest wenn es nach Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger geht. Wie sehr das dem Klima hilft, ist aber umstritten.

spiegel.title: Welche Zahl fehlt? - Rätsel der Woche
spiegel.description: Aus zwei Zahlen wird – auf welche Weise auch immer – eine dritte berechnet. Im Schema aus 13 Zahlen fehlt allerdings eine. Wie lautet sie?

spiegel.title: Helene Fischer kündigt neues Album für 2026 an: Vielleicht sogar ein bisschen »provokativ«
spiegel.description: Helene Fischer kündigt ein neues Album an – und das soll schon bald kommen. »WIR« soll es heißen und Altbekanntes liefern. Aber nicht nur.

spiegel.title: Leipzig: Flughafen äußert sich zu Sicherheitsvorgaben – Polizei ermittelt in alle Richtungen
spiegel.description: Wie kam es zu dem erneuten Sicherheitsvorfall am Flughafen Leipzig/Halle? Die Hintergründe sind unklar. Auch einen Unfall schließen die Behörden nicht aus, der Zaun liegt an einer öffentlich zugänglichen Straße.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Der Moment, in dem das historische Rathaus von Limoges einstürzt
spiegel.description: Ein Amateurvideo hält fest, wie das Dach des 140 Jahre alten Rathauses von Limoges einstürzt. Ein symbolträchtiger Augenblick am Abend eines Protesttags, der von Gewalt überschattet wurde.

spiegel.title: China: Lebenslange Haft nach Bleivergiftungen in Kindergarten
spiegel.description: Das Essen sollte appetitlicher aussehen. Dafür mischten Beschäftigte eines chinesischen Kindergartens bleihaltige Farbe unter die Mahlzeiten. Nun wurden sechs Menschen verurteilt.

observador.title: Carla Madeira e a ambiguidade moral do amor materno
observador.description: Antes, houve "Tudo é Rio", "A Natureza da Mordida" e "Véspera". Agora é a vez de "Quando": quando uma mãe vive a dúvida de denunciar ou não o filho? E nós bem no epicentro da narrativa.

observador.title: França em crise: Macron faz declaração esta noite
observador.description: Os protestos de sábado contra o aumento do custo de vida em França causaram centenas de milhões de euros em danos e um "número recorde" de detenções em Paris, diz a polícia.

observador.title: Cliente expulso de discoteca atinge a tiro um segurança
observador.description: Cliente terá sido expulso do estabelecimento por comportamento inadequado. Disparou sobre os seguranças, fazendo um ferido ligeiro.

observador.title: 13h. Número de detidos nas manifestações em França aumenta
observador.description: O Ministro do Interior divulgou que são mais de mil e oitocentos, e ainda é um número provisório. Ainda, um drone despenhou-se numa cidade no norte da Lituânia, junto da fronteira com a Letónia.

observador.title: Fokina bate Jodar na final do Masters de Xangai
observador.description: Tenista espanhol venceu em três sets o compatriota Rafael Jodar. Alejandro Davidovich Fokina conquistou assim pela primeira vez um Masters 1.000.

observador.title: Benfica quer renovar com Prestianni. Trubin sai em janeiro?
observador.description: Marco Silva arruma a casa. Francisco Moura ficou em xeque depois da derrota do FC Porto diante do Bétis? E o Sporting pode abdicar do capitão Gonçalo Inácio para o AC Milan de Ruben Amorim.

observador.title: 12h. Papa avisa que vai regressar gradualmente às atividades
observador.description: Líder da Igreja Católica fez a primeira oração do Angelus desde que foi operado. Ainda, Iuri Leitão e Ivo Oliveira conquistaram a medalha de prata nos Mundiais de pista em Xangai.

observador.title: Relógios, ténis, mobiliário: 23 lojas novas de norte a sul
observador.description: Da rua aos centros comerciais, incluindo formato outlet, várias marcas nacionais e estrangeiras abriram portas enquanto o país foi a banhos, e já na rentrée. Um guia das novidades.

observador.title: A corda entre Zelensky e Trump partiu de vez?
observador.description: No espaço de uma semana, Ucrânia enfrentou falhas no Starlink e nas informações militares vindas dos EUA. Trump, pressionado pelas intercalares, aponta a Zelensky. É um ponto de não-retorno?

observador.title: Papa reaparece na oração do Angelus, após operação
observador.description: Papa Leão XIV reapareceu em público, durante a oração do Angelus, da janela dos seus aposentos. Cirurgião diz que "não há motivos clínicos" para que Papa cancele viagem à América Latina.

observador.title: Cinco pistas e uma fatura: a TAP vai ter aterragem forçada?
observador.description: Entre pistas em Tancos, Beja e Alcochete, o país arrisca-se a ter mais aeroportos do que aviões no ar. Já os festejos da venda da TAP podem aterrar de emergência quando a fatura pública chegar.

observador.title: TAP. Governo quer oferta de capital para trabalhadores
observador.description: Depois da privatização, Pinto Luz diz que Governo espera poder lançar "no início de janeiro" a Oferta Pública de Venda (OPV) dos 5% do capital da TAP reservados aos trabalhadores.

observador.title: Incêndio em base canadiana causa vários mortos e feridos
observador.description: Um grave incêndio na base militar canadiana de Wainwright, na província de Alberta, causou mortos e feridos, de acordo com as autoridades, que ainda não precisaram o número de vítimas.

observador.title: 11h. Tendas mantêm-se no Rossio e na Praça D. João I
observador.description: Os manifestantes pedem habitação digna e tecem críticas às políticas do Governo de Luís Montenegro. E ainda, a imprensa canadiana diz que pelo sete pessoas morreram num incêndio numa base militar.

observador.title: Etapa de surf de Peniche suspensa por falta de condições
observador.description: Organização da etapa da Liga Mundial de Surf em Peniche vai estar parada domingo e segunda-feira, por falta de condições para retomar a competição.

observador.title: PJ detém em Évora homem foragido à Justiça
observador.description: Homem de 53 anos que estava foragido foi detido e vai cumprir uma pena de prisão de três anos e meio por crimes de recetação e detenção de arma proibida.

observador.title: "A Europa não consegue substituir os Estados Unidos"
observador.description: Madalena Meyer Resende, especialista em relações internacionais, avisa que a Europa não tem capacidade militar para substituir os Estados Unidos no apoio antiaéreo e de inteligência à Ucrânia.

phys-org.title: World's oldest shipwreck discovered off coast of Turkey
phys-org.description: A shipwreck off the coast of Turkey is the oldest shipwreck in the world, our team of archaeologists believes. There's little left of the ship itself, but based on clues from its cargo—including pottery vessels—a research team I was part of has tentatively dated the wreck to around 2700–2400 B.C.

phys-org.title: What a worm's brain can teach us about sex differences in the nervous system
phys-org.description: Ever wonder what goes on inside the brain of a worm—how it processes information, responds to stimuli and perceives the world around it? Northeastern University researchers have opened up that can of worms, specifically the one containing C. elegans, a tiny roundworm that's one of the most extensively studied animals in biology.

phys-org.title: How one of Earth's worst volcanic disasters affected societies in prehistoric Japan
phys-org.description: A new international study led by Lund University examines what happened to population levels after the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption in prehistoric Japan. The results paint a more complex picture than what had previously been believed. The paper is published in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Simulations explore nuclear mitigation of asteroid threats
phys-org.description: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) researchers are developing three-dimensional simulations to examine how a nuclear device could be used to deflect or potentially disrupt an asteroid threatening Earth.

phys-org.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
phys-org.description: Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

phys-org.title: What an ancient volcanic eruption teaches us about resilience today
phys-org.description: When a massive environmental disaster strikes, do societies simply collapse and disappear? Or do people find a way to adapt, rebuild and recover?

phys-org.title: Hand-cranked device tells blood type and red cell levels in 1 minute
phys-org.description: When someone is badly injured, doctors urgently need two facts: the patient's blood type, so that a transfusion is safe, and their hematocrit, the share of the blood made up of red blood cells, which reveals blood loss or anemia. Hospitals measure both with large machines that need electricity and trained staff, which are often unavailable in ambulances, disaster zones or remote clinics.

phys-org.title: Salt crystals could hold clues to life beneath Enceladus's ice
phys-org.description: The ocean beneath Saturn's moon Enceladus lies under kilometers of ice, but some of its contents do reach the surface. Jets near the south pole spray out water vapor and icy particles, offering a way to investigate the hidden ocean without drilling down to it.

phys-org.title: Australian scavengers don't just eat everything and slink away. They approach a carcass like a buffet
phys-org.description: When scientists talk about scavengers, you might imagine an animal sniffing out or stumbling across a carcass, eating as much as possible and slinking away.

phys-org.title: The ambiguous costs of climate change
phys-org.description: As human activity has increased temperatures globally, determining the costs directly incurred by climate change is challenging. The effects of climate change on extreme weather events—such as hurricanes and heat waves—can be locally specific and variable, and observations and climate modeling might not accurately capture those effects.

phys-org.title: Lone, starless cloud may be a 'dark' galaxy
phys-org.description: Astronomers using China's FAST radio telescope have discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it. This could be one of the strongest candidates yet for an isolated "dark galaxy," containing nearly 500,000 times the sun's mass in neutral hydrogen. The discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 24.

phys-org.title: Red-sensitive pigments in mantis shrimp eyes act as reversible light switches
phys-org.description: With about 30 visual pigments, compared to just three in humans, mantis shrimp possess a visual system that remains a mystery. Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, analyzed these pigments one by one and discovered that some detect red light that very few animals can perceive. This finding, published in Science Advances, has potential applications in optogenetics.

phys-org.title: Electrical sliding switches graphene between magnetic states
phys-org.description: In a discovery that could offer a new way to control quantum properties in two-dimensional materials, researchers at Cornell have found that electrically sliding the layers of ultrathin graphene can switch the material between distinct magnetic states that persist even after the voltage is removed.

phys-org.title: Global survey links financial hardship to lower trust in science
phys-org.description: Poor access to health care, limited local influence over research priorities and an unequal distribution of scientific benefits are undermining public confidence in science, experts warn, following the release of a global trust survey.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

proj-syn.title: A Global Euro Must First Win Over Europe
proj-syn.description: In a world of competing currency blocs, the euro is the dollar’s most credible rival. But for it to become a genuine counterweight to the greenback, the European Union must strengthen its financial foundations and expand its reach, starting with the member states that have not adopted it despite being obliged to do so.

proj-syn.title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
proj-syn.description: In 2012, when Japan was dealing with chronic deflation, policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates. Today, however, Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

proj-syn.title: A Middle-Powers Grand Strategy to Prevent Atrocities
proj-syn.description: Many governments have leverage to prevent atrocity crimes, yet lack the machinery to turn warnings into consistent, accountable action before it is too late. Now that three of the five permanent members of the Security Council are undercutting the postwar legal order, middle powers most close the gap.

proj-syn.title: Unleashing Africa’s Women Agripreneurs
proj-syn.description: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, women workers dominate agriculture but rarely capture the sector’s economic value. With a systematic approach to closing the gap, policymakers, NGOs, and philanthropic organizations could unlock a $1 trillion market and transform the continent’s food systems for the better.

proj-syn.title: Low Expectations for Israel’s Election
proj-syn.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel into a trap in which ever-increasing strategic commitments are outstripping the productive base that finances them, and the goodwill on which its alliances depend is being destroyed. While a new government would not transform Israeli foreign policy, it could begin to drag Israel out of its morass.

proj-syn.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
proj-syn.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

proj-syn.title: The Institutional Roots of Policy Nonsense
proj-syn.description: At a time when antimicrobial resistance threatens public health and our long-term economic well-being, tax policies favor financial engineering at the expense of developing new antibiotics. Similarly perverse incentives are at the heart of out-of-control public spending.

proj-syn.title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
proj-syn.description: Traditionally, Christian Democrats believed that taking care of all groups in society could create a harmonious balance that would prevent instability and self-destructive infighting. But the conditions that enabled this strategy have changed, particularly in Germany, where Christian Democrats must reconnect with a different part of their history.

proj-syn.title: Independent AI Auditing Now
proj-syn.description: Recent hacking incidents confirm the need for independent scrutiny not only of what AI systems are capable of, but also of what their developers are doing to minimize harm and communicate honestly with the public. Even if AI auditing is still at an early stage, other industries have already provided a playbook.

proj-syn.title: Strict Liability for AI Executives
proj-syn.description: As an OpenAI whistleblower recently explained, AI executives have knowingly fostered a culture that “guarantees periodic failures,” the scale of which is “growing as systems get more capable.” This approach hinges on an expectation of impunity, which is why AI firms must be held legally accountable for the harm their agents cause.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Pay to Preserve Tropical Forests?
proj-syn.description: For decades, the international community has acknowledged the extraordinary value of tropical forests while failing to invest adequately in their conservation. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, launched at last year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, could help close this financing gap.

proj-syn.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
proj-syn.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

proj-syn.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
proj-syn.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

proj-syn.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
proj-syn.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
proj-syn.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

proj-syn.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
proj-syn.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

proj-syn.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
proj-syn.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

proj-syn.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
proj-syn.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.
